name: walmsley2024_milk_evaporator
description: Two-effect MVR milk evaporator with milk heat treatment, 247 t/h raw milk (30 t/h milk powder); evaporation system in isolation. Loads in kW.
reference: Walmsley, Lincoln, Padullés, Cleland (2024), Energies 17, 2838, Table 2.

provenance.stream data: published (Table 2); Table 2 dT_cont used (chiller water 0.5 K; the text's pinch range implies 2.5 K, which leaves the targets unchanged)
provenance.eta_lorenz: published: 50 % exergetic (Carnot) efficiency (Sec. 4.2); reproduces the paper's simple-design COP 2.1
provenance.source_T_C: published: ambient / dead state 15 °C (Sec. 2), the source of the paper's simple design
provenance.sink levels: 105 °C published (simple design, Sec. 4.2.3); the 15-55 °C level is assumed (illustrative, follows the low-temperature part of the GCC)
provenance.economics: assumed: no economic data in the source (see economics.sources)
provenance.film coefficients: Stampfli et al. (2018) dairy values, stream mapping assumed
provenance.eta_lorenz_sensitivity: 0.45-0.52: Lorenz (Carnot) efficiencies implied by the DEA catalogue HTHP sheets 2.a/2.b (COP 4.45/2.75/2.4/2.05 at lifts of 40/65/80/100 K), as for the brewery
provenance.COP check: HTHP 105 °C (steam, 90 K lift): COP 2.10 vs DEA sheet 2.a 2.22 at 90 K minus 0.15 for steam = 2.07 (+1.5 %). Warm-water heat pump 15 -> 55 °C: Lorenz COP 7.86 vs DEA sheet 1.1 'up to 60 °C, lift 40 K' 5.33 (+47 %; the Lorenz model credits the full 40 K sink glide, which needs a glide-matched cycle such as transcritical CO2); with COP 5.33 RQ1 falls from 26 % to 23 %
provenance.steam sink: verified: the 105 °C level supplies the Direct Steam Injection that follows the 8 -> 95 °C preheat (Walmsley et al. 2024, Sec. 3.2), so the DEA steam-generation add-on applies

economics._note: No economic data in the source. Prices: Eurostat Portugal 2026-S1 for the site's consumption band at 8000 h/year; heat pump investment: Danish Energy Agency catalogue by sink temperature with its lift and steam add-ons; other parameters: tool defaults (Sources page). All are assumptions for this case.

The sheets' COP penalty for steam (-0.15) is not applied: COP comes from the Lorenz model

sources.prices: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 (gas) and nrg_pc_205 (electricity), Portugal, 2026-S1, excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes and levies, EUR/kWh, gas on GCV (data/sources/eurostat_portugal_prices.csv). The plant is not in Portugal: these prices place it in the dissertation's context. Bands: gas I3 0.0512, I4 0.0445, I5 0.0420; electricity ID 0.1135, IE 0.0897, IF 0.0789. Band check at 8000 h/year, site level (the site buys the energy): Walmsley et al. (2016), 'Total Site Utility Systems Optimisation for Milk Powder Production', CET 52, 235-240, DOI 10.3303/CET1652040: 30 t/h milk powder plant, electricity 210-220 kWh/t powder (literature 150-400), fuel 5,200 MJ/t powder (base case), and Walmsley et al. (2024): this evaporator belongs to a 30 t/h plant. Gas 5.2 GJ/t x 30 t/h x 8000 h = 1.25 million GJ (I5); electricity 220 kWh/t x 30 x 8000 = 52.8 GWh + heat pumps 11.7 GWh (IE). I4 below 6,400 h/year. Borderline gas band: the 5.2 GJ/t is the base-case fuel use; the improved design in the same paper (Table 1, design 1.0: 3.66 GJ/t thermal) gives 0.88 million GJ at 8000 h, band I4 (0.0445)
sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature, linear in capacity, plus the catalogue's add-ons for lift above 75 K (sink outlet minus source outlet) and steam generation (isothermal sinks). Replaces Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3), which is fitted to brewery heat pumps and gives 0.75-0.88 M€/MW for 2-3 MW units, below the catalogue range 0.9-1.5 M€/MW for sinks up to 125 °C. Indirect cost of new hot-water piping (0.23 M€/MW, 'relevant when needing to install new hot water piping instead of existing steam piping') is a scenario, not in the base
sources.chiller_cop: Sinnott and Towler (2020), Sec. 6.4.4, Eq. 6.20: real COP about 0.6 x Carnot (as for the brewery). Evaporator: chilled water leaves at 4 °C (Walmsley et al. 2024, Table 2) minus 5 K refrigerated-brine approach (Sec. 12.7.3: 3-5 K) = -1 °C; condenser 30 °C (ambient 15 °C + 10 K cooling-water rise + 5 K approach): 0.6 x 272.15/31 = 5.27. Q̇c,min (456 kW) is entirely this chilled-water load

area_targeting.film_coefficients_source: Stampfli et al. (2018), CET 70, 901-906, Table 1 (dairy plant): liquid product 500, water 2,000, evaporation/condensation 5,000 W/(m2 K). Mapping to these streams is our assumption: water for chiller water, CIP, direct-use water and cow water (milk condensate); product for raw milk and concentrate; condensation for vapour bleed, condenser and flash vapours

basis_hint: No operating hours are published for this plant. Milk supply varies considerably during the year (Atkins et al., 2009), so New Zealand milk-powder plants do not run all year: 8000 h/year is an upper bound. Price bands for this 30 t/h plant (Walmsley et al., 2016): gas I5 (0.0420 €/kWh) above 6,400 h/year, I4 (0.0445) below; electricity IE (0.0897) between 2,500 and 8,680 h/year. Change the prices in step 6 if you change the hours.

retrofit_bounds.note: Walmsley et al. (2024), Sec. 3.2 and Fig. 4: the base case derives from the heat-integrated 'ultra-low energy' design of Walmsley et al. (2018, Energy 146, 67-81) and the raw milk is preheated 8 -> 95 °C by heat recovery, but the exchangers are not listed. Use the lower bound; the exact existing network may be in Walmsley et al. (2018)
